title: Cloud agent box: guided tour
description: How your dotfiles, agents, Herdr, Tailscale, Moshi and Cua come together on a small Hetzner server that runs agents around the clock, and which settings you control.

props.content:
## The story

You rent one small Linux server in Germany, the **agent-box**. It runs the same setup as your Macs, installed from the same two repos: **dotfiles**, which covers the shell, tmux, Neovim and tools, and **agents**, which covers Pi, OpenCode, skills and Herdr.

Agents live in Herdr on that box and keep working when your laptop is closed. From the Mac, Herdr shows local and cloud agents in one window. From the phone, **Moshi** connects over Mosh and alerts you when an agent needs you. **Tailscale** is the only way in, and the box has no open public ports.

Later, **Cua** adds a virtual desktop on the box. Agents can drive it, and you can watch or take over from any browser.

*Status: research only. Nothing is provisioned yet. Knowledge base: `dotfiles/ai-artifacts/research/cloud-agent-box/`.*

props.title: 2. How you reach it, day to day
props.deck: Mac, phone and browser all reach the box over Tailscale.

props.content:
- Herdr keeps **Local** and **saved SSH machines** in one window. It shows a combined agent list and reconnects to each machine separately. Add `agent-box` next to the existing `herdr-home` and `herdr-work` launchers.
- The Herdr server lives on the box. If you close the lid or drop the network, the agents keep working.
- `ssh agent-box` uses Tailscale SSH, so there are no keys to copy.

- Moshi connects **directly** over SSH, Mosh or ET, with no relay.
- **Use Mosh.** It survives network switches and phone sleep. Its UDP ports are reachable only inside the tailnet.
- **moshi-hook** on the box sends approvals, notifications and status to one inbox, shows the agent conversation in a phone-native view, and opens dev servers in an in-app browser.
- It layers over Herdr, so the phone sees the same sessions as your Mac.

- `share-port 3000` on the box gives an HTTPS URL that only your tailnet can open. `local-web-gateway` is the only thing allowed to change Tailscale Serve.
- Persistent apps, such as OpenCode web, Plannotator, visual artifacts and the desktop viewer, become gateway routes.
- No **Funnel**, which makes URLs public, unless you choose it deliberately.

props.title: 3. Cost and billing
props.deck: Hourly pricing with a monthly cap. EU prices after the June 2026 change.

props.caption: € per month including VAT, with server, IPv4 and backups

rows.title: Hourly with a monthly cap
rows.body: You pay the lower of hours used times the hourly price, or the monthly price. Hetzner rounds up to whole hours.

rows.title: Stopped still costs
rows.body: You pay while the server exists. To stop paying, snapshot it, delete it and recreate it later.

rows.title: Traffic
rows.body: Incoming and internal traffic is free. 20 TB of outgoing traffic is included each month in the EU. After that, Hetzner bills in 100 MB blocks and warns you at 75% and 100%.

rows.title: Backups
rows.body: A flat 20% of the server price for automatic daily backups with 7 slots.

rows.title: Snapshots
rows.body: Taken by hand and billed per GB a month on compressed size.

rows.title: IPv4
rows.body: €0.50 a month. Keep it, because GitHub still has no IPv6.

rows.title: Price risk
rows.body: Hetzner raised prices on 1 April and again on 15 June 2026.

props.title: 4. Uptime and what survives a restart
props.deck: Treat the box as disposable. The repos and 1Password can rebuild it.

props.content:
- Automatic security updates, with **reboots at 04:00 only when needed**.
- Herdr starts at boot as a systemd user service with linger, so it comes back without a login.
- Daily Hetzner backups while the setup is new.
- Aim to **rebuild in under an hour**. Code lives in git, config in dotfiles and agents, and secrets in 1Password.
- Hetzner announces scheduled maintenance at least 24 hours ahead.

props.title: 6. Computer use with Cua
props.deck: A virtual desktop that agents drive and you can watch or take over.

items.title: You, on a Mac or phone

props.content:
**One-day spike:** run a desktop container with Chromium and noVNC. Install `cua-driver` and run `cua-driver doctor`. Connect Pi over MCP. Complete the calculator tutorial (6 × 7 = 42), then one real task. Open the viewer from the phone. Write down RAM and CPU use and make a go or no-go decision.

**Estimate, not yet measured:** the desktop with Chromium uses about 1.5 to 3 GB of RAM. On a CX33 that leaves room for 2 to 4 command-line agents. Move to a CX43 if the desktop stays running all the time.

**Use agent-browser for simple web tasks.** It's lighter. Use the full desktop only for real GUI apps or a shared, logged-in browser.

props.title: 7. Plan and risks
props.deck: Each phase ends in a working state you can check.

props.body: Create the Hetzner server, which costs money. Create the 1Password service account and vault. Approve the Tailscale ACL change. Install Moshi and Tailscale on the phone if they aren't there yet.
